judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: A link in the header to WhatsApp (api.whatsapp.com) whose only content is the WhatsApp logo image (icone_whatsapp_sem_fundo, alt=""). The "Fale com a SBH:" figcaption sits outside the link. The screenshot pixels give the green glyph #00e676/#00e777 on white at 1.68:1, so the claim is true of the capture, and the live page has the same markup and image. Whether this fails 1.4.11 turns on the logo exemption. Understanding 1.4.11 says "Logos are exempted from contrast requirements" and, for a logo used as a link, only that authors "as a best practice" should consider a variant with enough contrast. It also says a low-contrast presentation chosen by the author, not mandated by brand guidelines, is not essential and so not exempt. WhatsApp's green mark is low-contrast on white even in its official colour, but monochrome variants exist. So one auditor would exempt it as a brand logo and another would fail it under G207. My lean is that it passes under the logo exemption, but competent auditors would reasonably disagree, so the label is uncertain. Separately, the link has no accessible name (empty alt, no aria-label or title), which fails 1.1.1, 2.4.4 and 4.1.2; this finding does not claim that.
